newsitem.title: USA: Hartford leaders in talks to save hockey team.
newsitem.headline: Hartford leaders in talks to save hockey team.

text.p: A group of Hartford business and civic leaders are making a last-ditch effort to keep the Whalers hockey team in Connecticut's capital city, Hartford Mayor Mike Peters said on Monday.

Peter Karmanos, who owns the National Hockey League (NHL) franchise, last week rejected Connecticut Gov. John Rowland's proposal to build a $147 million arena and said the team would leave the state at the end of this season.
Hartford leaders are ready to float a $20 million bond to help defray expected team losses while the team awaits a new arena, Peters told Reuters.
"It's still a long shot," he said. "(But) we want to make sure that every rock has been turned over, to make sure we haven't missed anything." The outcome should be known within three days, he said.
The Whalers came to Hartford in 1975 and joined the NHL four years later. The team is Connecticut's only major league sports franchise.
The basic details of the proposal to keep the Whalers in Hartford would be very similar to Rowland's offer, Peters said.
"I don't mean we're going to be going overboard here, but... maybe there's a couple of little things in here that might turn the tide, so we're going to work on it," he said.
Gov. Rowland, a Republican, was not involved in the talks on Monday, his press secretary Dean Pagani said.

"If people want to make an effort to put some kind of offer together, they can go ahead and do that," Pagani said. "But we should point out that the governor has been working on this issue for between six months and a year, and he feels many of these avenues have been exhausted."

"As for today's developments... I've just been saying that this last week, Peter Karmanos made very clear that he wants to move his team at the end of this season, and there's no reason to believe that he's changed his mind," Pagani said.
